full_caption: Foxglove Landing Municipal Housing Authority, Appellant, v. Two Rivers Development Partners, L.P., Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: This appeal concerns a claimed easement of access across the northern 16 feet of the parcel at 31 Kingfisher Drive, Harrowgate, MD, owned by Two Rivers Development Partners, L.P., in favor of the landlocked rear parcel owned by Foxglove Landing Municipal Housing Authority.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The common grantor conveyed the rear parcel in 1990 without any reservation of a right of way. At that time the rear parcel abutted the abandoned rail grade, which was subsequently vacated by the Harrowgate County Board, leaving the parcel without lawful access.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The evidence showed that Foxglove Landing Municipal Housing Authority and predecessors drove a gravel track across the servient estate from 1990 through 2000, maintained it with periodic grading, and installed a culvert at the drainage swale in 2016.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: An easement appurtenant runs with the land and passes on conveyance of the dominant estate whether or not it is mentioned in the deed. It is extinguished only by release, merger, abandonment, or prescription running against it.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: An easement by necessity arises where (1) the dominant and servient estates were formerly held in common ownership, (2) that unity was severed, and (3) the necessity for the way existed at the moment of severance. Necessity arising afterward will not support the easement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Acts of maintenance visible to the servient owner are strong evidence that the use was under a claim of right rather than by neighborly accommodation. The grading and culvert installation here satisfy that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Abandonment requires more than mere non-use. There must be an affirmative act evincing an intent to relinquish the right permanently. The fifteen years of non-use shown here, standing alone, does not extinguish the easement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Because the want of access arose from the later vacation of a public road rather than from the severance itself, no easement by necessity was created. The trial court's contrary conclusion was error.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: An easement by prescription requires use that is open, notorious, continuous, hostile and under a claim of right for the full statutory period of 15 years. Permissive use, however long continued, never ripens into a prescriptive right.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The judgment declaring a prescriptive easement is affirmed as to the way as historically used, and modified to exclude the proposed commercial expansion. Costs to Two Rivers Development Partners, L.P..

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — GRANT AND DESCRIPTION OF EASEMENT
sections.text: Grantor grants to Grantee, its successors and assigns, a perpetual non-exclusive easement 16 feet in width for ingress, egress and utilities over and across the northerly portion of the Servient Estate, the centerline of which is the existing gravel drive as it presently exists on the ground. This easement is appurtenant to and runs with the Dominant Estate and may not be conveyed separately from it.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Marrowdale.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Marrowdale, the period is extended to the next business day.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Indemnity
sections.text: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from all claims, damages and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of that party's use of the subject premises or breach of this instrument, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the party seeking indemnity. This clause survives termination.
